title: skip-level-catch-up-notes-maya-kapur-jul07-2026
content:
Meeting: skip-level 1:1 with Diego Ramos (IC3) — 2026-07-07 10:00am PT
Location: Zoom / Diego's desk
Duration: 30m
Objective: quick alignment on priorities and unblockers; coaching checkin; short-term execution focus for next sprint

Agenda (proposed, keep flexible)
1) Quick pulse (3m) — how are things? energy, focus, blockers
2) Delivery + priorities (8m)
   - INF-4821 rollout status (quantized fp16 path): confirm current perf impact and deployment window
   - PR #938 merge readiness: e2e tests failing on long-seq kernels — what's needed to green?
   - Cost/runway: Diego mentioned token cost anomaly last week — short summary and hypothesis
3) Technical tradeoffs (7m)
   - quantization vs. KV-cache correctness: acceptable perf envelope for canary customers?
   - any concerns about the fallback routing policy (region->capacity-tier) for Dedicated during bursts
4) Career / growth (6m)
   - shadowing plan for infra-oncall handoff; want to create a 4-week ramp doc
   - interest in leading the evals for model-variant A/B (small experiment leadership)
5) Action items + quick wins (6m)
   - surface next steps and owners, confirm due dates

Pre-meeting notes / what I want to learn from Diego (scratchpad)
- Status on INF-4821: he ran internal load tests Friday but still sees higher  tail latency when sequence > 2048. Need concrete failure mode (OOM vs scheduling latency).
- Who's blocked on PR #938? Looks like test infra is flaky; maybe sandbox version mismatch (cuda/cu version). Ask Diego to call out needed infra help.
- Cost issue: tokens per-request spiked for a subset of evals — ask if cache invalidation policy changed or a misrouted model variant caused dequantization.
- Team bandwidth: Diego's time split across bugfixes and canary rollout. Need to decide if we postpone the QoS refactor this sprint.
- Coaching: Diego is interested in moving toward owning small cross-team projects. Suggest 1 micro-lead assignment (A/B eval) + pair on stakeholder comms.

Draft talking points (concise)
- "Thanks for shipping the batching optimization — it improved median latency. For rollout, let's prioritize tail latency fixes before wide canary."
- "If test infra is the blocker, escalate to infra-qa and I'll pull Tim for a quick sync."
- "For your growth plan: run the A/B eval end-to-end; I'll co-own the stakeholder memo and give feedback on comms."

Open questions to cover
- Is the tail latency reproducible locally, or only in Dedicated canary under multi-tenant load?
- Does the quantized kernel cause slight degradation on outputs we care about? Any eval regressions tied to prompts in the production prompt set?
- Are there any PR blockers that require cross-team permission (infra, release-engineering)?

Action items (write down during meeting)
- Diego: attach latest long-seq flamegraphs to INF-4821 by EOD 2026-07-07 (owner: Diego Ramos, due: 2026-07-07)
- Maya: open infra-qa ticket and tag Tim for test infra instability; propose a 30m triage session 2026-07-08 (owner: Maya Kapur, due: 2026-07-08)
- Diego: reduce canary rollout size to 10% and add extra logging around KV-cache invalidations; report impact by 2026-07-09 (owner: Diego Ramos, due: 2026-07-09)
- Diego + Maya: draft a 4-week ramp doc for oncall handoff and runbook edits; first draft by 2026-07-14 (owner: Diego Ramos, collaborator: Maya Kapur, due: 2026-07-14)
- Maya: offer micro-lead for A/B eval and draft stakeholder comms template by 2026-07-10 (owner: Maya Kapur, due: 2026-07-10)

Notes for follow-up (post-meeting)
- If Diego confirms OOMs, consider bumping Dedicated instance memory or change batch sizing heuristic for long-seq requests. Schedule a short change window with release-engineering.
- If PR #938 is blocked by test infra, ask release-engineering for temporary runner allocation; we can also backport a flaky-test-fix branch.
- Track token-cost anomaly: add a small Grafana dashboard panel for token-rate/embedding-rate per model-variant so we can quickly spot regressions next sprint.

Coaching / feedback items to deliver gently if needed
- Encourage Diego to call out when a task is drifting; prefer a short comment in ticket rather than silent context switching.
- Praise: highlight recent batching improvement and clear commit messages — call out ownership in the team channel.

Quick reference links (to paste into Slack during the call)
- JIRA: INF-4821 (quantized rollout) — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821
- GH PR: serving-runtime PR #938 — https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/938
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime — thread about canary anomalies — https://app.slack.com/client/T12345/C67890/thread/1654321

Misc scratch / TODO list (not for meeting unless relevant)
- Follow up with Tim on test runner capacity and a temporary GPU allocation for long-seq tests.
- Draft a short postmortem template for canary regressions (1 page) — include signal checklist: latency, tokens, accuracy evals, error rates.
- Add Diego to the billing alert for token-cost spikes so he gets alerts during the night shift.

Tone notes: keep 1:1 collaborative and action-oriented. Avoid over-prescribing — give Diego ownership of the technical path but offer removal of blockers.

End of doc.
